BmsHistoryRecord.description: 64-byte history record: ten of them follow the status snapshot inside the journal record. Offsets are relative to the start of the record. bms_history_ring_commit fills all ten on its first call and later shifts them down one slot per commit.

fields.name: timestamp
fields.description: Timestamp taken for the commit by bms_4168_08009d84 (a clock or tick read whose name is not given).

fields.name: status_words
fields.description: 13 u16 words copied from the status block at +0x140 (word i comes from +0x140 + 2*i).

fields.name: status_s16_11a
fields.description: Signed 16-bit value from the status block at +0x11A.

fields.name: low_bytes
fields.description: Low bytes of the u16 words at +0x12C, +0x12E, +0x130, +0x134, +0x136 and +0x138, in that order. Only the low byte of each word is kept.

fields.name: status_11e
fields.description: Byte at +0x11E of the status block.

fields.name: status_19c
fields.description: Byte at +0x19C of the status block.

fields.name: status_124_126
fields.description: u16 at +0x124 (low half) and u16 at +0x126 (high half) as one 32-bit word. Its bits are the status flags mirrored by bms_status_event_snapshot.

fields.name: status_194_196
fields.description: u16 at +0x194 (low half) and u16 at +0x196 (high half) as one 32-bit word.

fields.name: status_13c
fields.description: u16 at +0x13C. In the first-call loop of bms_history_ring_commit it is stored at 0x200010EC + 0x20*k rather than at the 0x40 record stride, so for k of 1 or more it lands in an earlier record (probably a firmware stride bug). Later commits write the newest record correctly.

fields.name: status_13e
fields.description: u16 at +0x13E. Same stride problem as status_13c (first-call loop stores it at record base + 0x20*k).

fields.name: status_180
fields.description: Byte at +0x180 of the status block.

fields.name: status_1d2
fields.description: Byte at +0x1D2 of the status block.

BmsJournalRecord.description: 660-byte (0x294) record that bms_extflash_journal_step writes to external flash. A 20-byte status snapshot comes first, then ten BmsHistoryRecord entries. The newest history record is at 0x200012FC.

fields.name: snap_flags
fields.description: Status flag byte mirrored from 0x2000056B by bms_status_event_snapshot. Each bit is one status condition, and the snapshot is taken when a flag rises.

fields.name: snap_timestamp
fields.description: 32-bit timestamp from bms_4168_08009d84, stored when the snapshot is taken.

fields.name: snap_u16_118
fields.description: u16 at +0x118 of the status block at snapshot time.

fields.name: snap_s16_11a
fields.description: s16 at +0x11A of the status block at snapshot time.

fields.name: snap_byte_dfc
fields.description: Byte read from 0x20000DFC when the snapshot is taken (the object there is not described in this packet).

fields.name: snap_u16_b4
fields.description: u16 at +0xB4 of the status block at snapshot time.

fields.name: snap_u16_b6
fields.description: u16 at +0xB6 of the status block at snapshot time.

fields.name: snap_status_word
fields.description: u16 at +0x124 and u16 at +0x126 as one 32-bit word at snapshot time.

fields.name: history
fields.description: Ten history records (64 bytes each). Record 0 is the oldest and record 9, at 0x200012FC, is the newest. Each commit shifts records 1 to 9 down by one and writes a fresh record 9.
